source_title: Protection from Stalking, Sexual Assault or Human Trafficking Act — Definitions (Unmanned Aerial System Harassment)
citation: K.S.A. 60-31a02 (UAS language added by L. 2016, ch. 58, §3)
revision_date: 2018-07-01 (L. 2018, ch. 110, §5 — most recent amendment; unrelated to the UAS text)
regulated_party: Any person (private/commercial operators and the general public)
regulated_activity: Using an unmanned aerial system to carry out a course of conduct over or near a dwelling, occupied vehicle, or other place where a person may reasonably expect to be safe from uninvited intrusion or surveillance, as part of stalking/harassment
requirement_type: Prohibition (element of civil stalking protective-order relief under the Act; not a standalone UAS criminal statute)
summary: K.S.A. 60-31a02, part of the Protection from Stalking, Sexual Assault or Human Trafficking Act, defines "harassment" to expressly include "any course of conduct carried out through the use of an unmanned aerial system over or near any dwelling, occupied vehicle or other place where one may reasonably expect to be safe from uninvited intrusion or surveillance" (subsection (d)(1)). The section separately defines "unmanned aerial system" (subsection (e)) using FAA-derived criteria (powered, no onboard human operator, aerodynamic lift, autonomous or remotely piloted, expendable or recoverable, lethal or nonlethal payload). The UAS language was added by a 2016 amendment (L. 2016, ch. 58, §3) and has not been altered since.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Plan environmental and mapping flights to avoid conduct that could be characterized as locating, pursuing, disturbing, or harassing wildlife. Coordinate mission timing and stand-off distances with the land manager when project work overlaps sensitive habitat or hunting activity.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: N/A — no procurement or equipment-selection implication identified
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Treat the cited authority as a documented compliance gate where applicable. Preserve the facts supporting any exception or consent theory, allocate client and operator responsibilities clearly, and seek state counsel when project facts approach ambiguous or penal language.
verification_status: Full current section text verified directly against the official Kansas Office of the Revisor of Statutes website (ksrevisor.gov); the section's own history note confirms the 2016 UAS-language amendment (L. 2016, ch. 58, §3), and the citation was independently cross-checked against the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks' own official FAQ page, which cites this same section for the same proposition.
notes: "Harassment" requires a "course of conduct" (two or more acts evidencing continuity of purpose) under subsection (d)(2), so a single, isolated UAS overflight is not by itself "stalking" under this Act, though it may still support other legal claims (e.g., trespass). AEC operators should document consent/notice for flights near occupied residences given this statute's express reference to UAS.

source_title: Motorized Vehicles and Aircraft; Authorized Operation — KDWP Lands and Waters (Drone/UAS Use Construed as Prohibited per Official KDWP Guidance)
citation: K.A.R. 115-8-13 (authorized by and implementing K.S.A. 2015 Supp. 32-807); construed by KDWP's official "Drones/Unmanned Aircraft Systems" FAQ (ksoutdoors.gov)
source_type: Binding regulation, supplemented by official agency guidance
binding_level: Binding (regulation); Advisory guidance (KDWP's construction extending it to drones)
uas_topic: UAS operation prohibited on state park/wildlife-area/state-fishing-lake land, via agency construction of a general aircraft-landing rule
regulated_party: Any person (private/commercial operators and the general public) on KDWP-owned or managed property
regulated_activity: Operating a drone/UAS (including for photography, mapping, filming, or inspection) on any KDWP-owned or managed property, absent a designated operating area or the secretary's authorization

summary: K.A.R. 115-8-13(d) provides only that "motorized aircraft landings and takeoffs shall be allowed in designated areas only or as authorized by the secretary"; the regulation's own text does not mention "drone," "UAS," or "unmanned aircraft." The same FAQ states that a list of parks with designated drone operating areas is "in development," implying none are currently designated.

source_title: Unlawful Methods of Taking Wildlife (Aircraft) — KDWP Construction Applying the Statute to Drone-Aided Hunting, Scouting, and Game Recovery
citation: K.S.A. 32-1003(a)(1)-(2) (most recently amended L. 2005, ch. 182, §4); construed by KDWP's official drone/hunting FAQ (ksoutdoors.gov) and the 2025-2026 Kansas Hunting & Furharvesting Regulations Summary
source_type: Binding law or regulation, supplemented by official agency guidance
revision_date: 2005-07-01 (statute); current as of the 2025-2026 season (KDWP guidance)
binding_level: Binding (statute); Advisory guidance (KDWP's construction extending "air vehicle" to drones, and related "take"/game-recovery guidance)
uas_topic: UAS-aided hunting, scouting, and game-recovery restriction (wildlife/hunting)
regulated_activity: Taking (or providing/receiving location information to aid in taking) a game or furbearing animal from an airplane or other air vehicle; using a drone to scout, locate wounded or harvested game, or film a hunt on KDWP land
permit_or_approval_required: N/A (the statutory handicapped-hunting-permit exception under K.S.A. 32-931 is unrelated to UAS)
commercial_operator_relevance: Yes — but KDWP guidance limits this to hunting-related UAS activity, not general commercial UAS use
summary: K.S.A. 32-1003(a)(1) makes it unlawful to take a game or furbearing animal "from a motorboat, airplane, motor vehicle or other water, air or land vehicle" absent a handicapped-hunting permit issued under K.S.A. 32-931; (a)(2) separately bars providing or receiving an animal's location "by radio or other mechanical device for purposes of taking" it. Neither provision names "drone" or "UAS." KDWP's official FAQ (ksoutdoors.gov) states directly that "the use of drones (UASs/UAVs) for hunting or scouting is prohibited in Kansas," citing this section and the federal Airborne Hunting Act (16 U.S.C. §742j-1), and separately states a drone may not be used to locate wounded or harvested game (citing the "take" definition at K.S.A. 32-701) or to film a hunt on KDWP-owned/managed land.

notes: PENDING BILL: House Bill 2423 (2026), the "Kansas Wounded Deer Recovery Act," would amend K.S.A. 32-1003 to allow FAA-licensed drone operators (with landowner permission) to use a drone solely to locate wounded or recently deceased deer, while continuing to bar drone use to harass or pursue wildlife. Per the Kansas Legislature's official bill-status tracker (fetched directly), HB 2423 is currently shown with a status of "Died" following a January 27, 2026 House Federal and State Affairs Committee hearing; it has not been enacted, and current law (as construed by KDWP) continues to bar drone use to locate harvested or wounded game. Relevance to AEC work is limited to wildlife-survey or agricultural-monitoring UAS flights conducted during hunting seasons.

source_title: Acquisition of Certain Drones or Related Components, Services, or Equipment by Governmental Agencies Prohibited; Exceptions
citation: K.S.A. 75-3740h and 75-3740i (2025 Session Laws, ch. 68 [House Substitute for Senate Bill 9], §§12-13)
uas_topic: State/local-government drone procurement restriction — critical infrastructure / country-of-concern / foreign-principal security restriction
regulated_party: Governmental agencies (the state or any political or taxing subdivision, or any office, agency, or instrumentality thereof) — public agency only
regulated_activity: Purchasing or acquiring a drone, or related services, maintenance agreements, or equipment, whose critical components (including installed software) were produced in a "country of concern" (China/Hong Kong, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Venezuela) or produced/owned by a "foreign principal"
requirement_type: Prohibition, with a grandfather clause for pre-July 1, 2025 equipment and a narrow safety/security-necessity exception requiring secretary of administration approval
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — secretary of administration approval (after consultation with the adjutant general) required to invoke the narrow necessity exception under subsection (c)
commercial_operator_relevance: Indirect — governs public-agency purchasing, not private commercial operators directly, but may flow down through state/local contract specifications
summary: K.S.A. 75-3740h bars a "governmental agency" from purchasing or acquiring any drone, or related services/maintenance/equipment, whose critical components were produced in a "country of concern" or produced/owned by a "foreign principal," as those terms are defined in the companion definitions section, K.S.A. 75-3740i. Equipment acquired before July 1, 2025 may continue in use; a narrow exception allows an otherwise-prohibited acquisition where no other reasonable means exists, the secretary of administration approves after consulting the adjutant general, and the safety/security risk of not acquiring exceeds the risk of the prohibited acquisition. Enacted as Sections 12-13 of the 2025 House Substitute for Senate Bill 9 (2025 Session Laws, ch. 68), signed by Governor Kelly on April 7, 2025.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Track this authority before mobilization, but do not treat a proposal, repealed measure, or superseded source as a current operating rule. Base the flight plan on the verified law and agency policy then in force.
practical_interpretation_agency_practiti: Before proposing equipment or mobilizing, ask Kansas Legislature which current list, funding determination, exception request, or project-level confirmation controls. Provide the aircraft, payload, controller, software, manufacturer/origin, and contract information the agency requests and retain its written determination with the procurement and flight records.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: Before bidding public work, obtain vendor documentation for aircraft, critical components, installed software, ownership, and origin; compare it with current client solicitations and official lists. Do not assume the public-agency restriction automatically binds the AEC consultant.
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Separate current law from legislative or historical context in advice and contract documents. Recheck status at project kickoff and before mobilization, and avoid representing a proposal, vetoed measure, or superseded source as binding.
verification_status: Full current text of both K.S.A. 75-3740h and 75-3740i verified directly against the official Kansas Office of the Revisor of Statutes website; each section's history note confirms enactment as 2025 ch. 68, §§12 and 13 respectively. The enrolled 2025 House Substitute for Senate Bill 9 was independently verified in full against the Kansas Secretary of State's official 2025 Session Laws publication (sos.ks.gov), including the Governor's April 7, 2025 approval date.
notes: MATERIAL LEGISLATIVE-HISTORY / CITATION-DISCREPANCY FINDING (see also KS-007): this restriction did NOT originate from, and was never enacted as, House Bill 2293 (2025) standing alone — HB 2293 (Rep. Croft) is shown "Died" on the Kansas Legislature's official bill tracker; its substantive drone-procurement language was instead folded by the House Commerce, Labor and Economic Development Committee into a substitute for an unrelated bill, Senate Bill 9 (originally concerning foreign-principal land acquisition near military installations), which passed as amended and was signed into law. A near-identical 2024 predecessor, House Substitute for Senate Bill 271, passed both chambers in 2024 but was VETOED by Governor Kelly on April 24, 2024, and the Senate's April 29, 2024 motion to override the veto failed (21-16, short of the two-thirds required), sustaining the veto — SB 271 (2024) never became law. Secondary sources describing "SB 271" as Kansas's current drone-procurement law, without noting the veto and the 2025 re-enactment via Sub. for SB 9, are describing a bill that died in 2024; the correct current citation is K.S.A. 75-3740h/75-3740i.

citation: K.S.A. 74-7003(t) (Definitions, State Board of Technical Professions Act); K.A.R. 66-12-1 (Minimum Standards for the Practice of Professional Surveying)
source_type: Binding law or regulation (statute and rule) — general licensing framework only
effective_date: Unknown original enactment (Board of Technical Professions Act); most recently amended L. 2015, ch. 78, §1
binding_level: Binding (general licensing framework only — no UAS-specific rule or guidance identified)
uas_topic: General professional-licensing competency for photogrammetric/surveying methods (no UAS-specific rule or guidance located)
regulated_party: Licensed professional surveyors; persons performing professional surveying services
regulated_activity: Practicing professional surveying — defined to include use of "mathematics, geodesy and photogrammetry," geometric measurement, boundary determination, and creating/modifying electronic or computerized survey data — without licensure
permit_or_approval_required: License (professional surveyor) generally required for the practice of professional surveying as defined
summary: K.S.A. 74-7003(t) defines "professional surveying" to include, among other things, use of "mathematics, geodesy and photogrammetry" and the making of geometric measurements to determine boundaries, positions, and configurations of the earth's surface, plus "creating, preparing or modifying electronic, computerized or other data" relative to those activities. The definition is method-neutral apart from its express reference to photogrammetry; it does not reference UAS, drones, or LiDAR by name. No standalone rule, advisory opinion, or FAQ from the Kansas State Board of Technical Professions specifically addressing UAS-derived photogrammetric or LiDAR survey products was located during this research pass; the Board's public surveyor-resources page (ksbtp.ks.gov) covers licensure, exams, and continuing education, with no UAS-specific content.
